summary.text: A boy, the first child of non-consanguineous parents, was born by cesarean section at 37 weeks of gestation because of breech presentation, with Apgar score 9/10, birth weight 3090 g and discreetly icteric skin. Prelingual speech phases were reduced, the lingual phase was delayed and early motor development was discretely atypical; he did not crawl and walked at 18 months. A first BERA at 29 months suggested a right-ear deficit, later considered possibly influenced by EEG instability.

At 38 months he was brought to the speech pathology institute, where he showed limited verbal expression, resisted cooperation and displayed symptoms consistent with ASD. The admission team diagnosed ASD. Repeated BERA at 36 and 38 months showed average hearing thresholds bilaterally and no need for amplification. MRT showed small bilateral periventricular, peritrigonal and supratentorial scarring lesions, and white matter signal abnormalities were reported alongside ASD.

Integrative therapy based on the KSAFA approach was delivered over two and a half years, with Sensory Profile 2, ADOS-2, cognitive testing, SEPAC and EEG recordings repeated at 38, 44, 54, 60 and 66 months. Sensory Profile 2 scores moved toward average values, while TIQ fell, SEPAC-estimated developmental ages rose but lagged calendar age, and ADOS-2 scores stayed above the autism spectrum critical value. EEG showed rising relative theta and falling relative alpha during the cartoon.

At 60 months MRT findings were similar to the first study. At 66 months he became verbal with inconsistent single words, echolalia, persisting motor stereotypes and attention deficit, and neurological examination showed axial hypotonia and weakness of the orofacial musculature. Cognitive testing indicated mild intellectual disability at 66 months. Overall, the authors report poor and insufficient improvement despite intensive treatment.
